t: V Programming Language net.http TLS Certificate Validation Bypass
d: V programming language standard library net.http through version 0.5.2 prior to commit 4077484 contains a TLS certificate validation bypass vulnerability that allows on-path attackers to intercept HTTPS traffic by exploiting the default false value of SSLConnectConfig.validate and FetchConfig.validate, which completes TLS handshakes without verifying certificates in both the mbedtls and OpenSSL backends. Attackers can present an expired, self-signed, wrong-hostname, or untrusted-root certificate to successfully complete the handshake via http.get, http.post, or http.fetch, enabling interception or modification of HTTPS traffic unless validate: true is explicitly configured.

t: Unbounded HTTP/3 Datagram flow map growth in tokio-quiche
d: Summary Cloudflare tokio-quiche was found to contain an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in its HTTP/3 DATAGRAM handling. For every previously unseen flow identifier (quarter stream ID) received in a DATAGRAM frame, tokio-quiche creates and retains new, per-flow state. A remote peer can send DATAGRAMs with many distinct identifiers, causing the per-connection flow map and associated channel state to grow without bound. Impact Exploitation can exhaust process memory and cause a denial of service. The vulnerable code is used in both client and server configurations, so either role can be affected by a malicious peer. QUIC DATAGRAM support in tokio-quiche is enabled by default through QuicSettings::enable_dgram; applications can disable it by setting this field to false. The vulnerable HTTP/3 path is reachable only when DATAGRAM support is negotiated with the peer. Core quiche and HTTP/3 deployments without DATAGRAM support are not affected. Mitigation Disable DATAGRAMs in tokio-quiche’s QuicSettings::enable_dgram. Remediation Upgrade to tokio-quiche version 0.23.0 or later. The fixed code creates flow state only for valid DATAGRAM-capable request streams, which are bounded by QUIC’s stream limits. To tolerate packet reordering, servers retain early DATAGRAMs in a bounded, expiring buffer, while clients discard DATAGRAMs for unknown flows.

t: Busybox: heap buffer overflow in wget ftp resume when the resume offset exceeds the reported file size
d: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When resuming a download over File Transfer Protocol (FTP), the wget utility fails to verify that the resume offset does not exceed the file size reported by the server, resulting in an integer calculation error. A malicious FTP server or an on-path network attacker can exploit this issue by returning crafted file size metadata, triggering a heap-based buffer overflow with attacker-controlled data. Successful exploitation may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code or crash the application, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

t: MISP sourcecache module SSRF allows fetching arbitrary internal URLs via attribute enrichment
d: The sourcecache expansion module in MISP Modules (misp-modules) contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. When a user with permission to create or modify attributes of type 'link' or 'url' submits an attribute value, the module passes the URL directly to its internal archiving function without any validation of the target address. An attacker can therefore craft a URL pointing to loopback addresses (e.g., 127.0.0.1), private network ranges, link-local addresses, or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., 169.254.169.254). The MISP server will issue an HTTP request to that target and store the response body in the event, effectively exfiltrating data from internal services to the attacker through the MISP interface. Non-HTTP schemes such as file:// are also accepted, potentially allowing local file disclosure. The vulnerability requires an authenticated MISP user with the ability to create or edit attributes of the affected types. The security impact is information disclosure from internal services reachable by the MISP server, including sensitive data such as cloud credentials, internal application data, or local files.

t: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in the Vaadin Rich Text Editor via an Unescaped Video Embed
d: The Vaadin Rich Text Editor exports a video embed without escaping its value, and then parses the resulting HTML into live DOM. A value crafted to break out of the href attribute therefore runs script in the viewer's browser. An attacker who can edit shared content pastes a video embed carrying the payload, the delta is stored, and the script runs when any user opens the page, including in read only mode. Only content persisted through asDelta() is affected. The default HTML value, set and read through setValue and getValue, is sanitized on the server with a safelist that has no iframe, so the embed does not survive that path. Vaadin 24 and older are not affected: they build the HTML value from the editor's own innerHTML, which the browser escapes. Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include: Product version Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13 Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13 Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12 Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4 Mitigation No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer Upgrade to 25.2.13 Upgrade to 25.3.5

t: Unescaped Download File Name Allows Content-Disposition Parameter Injection in Vaadin Flow
d: DownloadEvent.setFileName(String) in Vaadin Flow writes the download file name into the Content-Disposition header without escaping it. When the name is pure US-ASCII the header is built as attachment; filename="<name>" with the name inserted verbatim, so a double quote in the name ends the quoted string early and the rest of the name is read by the browser as further header parameters. The inline(String) variant, present from Vaadin 25.0, builds the name the same way. An application that passes an untrusted file name to either method, for example when re-serving a file under the name it was uploaded with, lets an attacker add a filename* parameter. Browsers prefer filename* over filename, so the file is saved under a name and extension of the attacker's choosing, which defeats any file name or extension restriction the application enforces. The attacker cannot change the attachment or inline disposition itself and cannot split the header. Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include: Product version Vaadin 24.8.0 - 24.8.17 Vaadin 24.9.0 - 24.9.25 Vaadin 24.10.0 - 24.10.13 Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13 Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13 Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12 Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4 Mitigation No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 24.9.26 or newer Upgrade to 24.9.26 Upgrade to 24.10.14 No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer Upgrade to 25.2.13 Upgrade to 25.3.5 Vaadin versions below 24.8 are not affected: the DownloadEvent API does not exist in them.

t: Libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on i/o error.
d: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

t: Gst-plugins-bad: gst-plugins-bad: off-by-one write in mxf demuxer temporal offset table
d: A flaw was found in GStreamer's MXF demuxer. When an application processes a crafted MXF file, an off-by-one bounds check can allow a one-byte write past the logical end of a temporal offset array. This may corrupt memory and cause the application to crash. The extent of the impact has not been demonstrated by a runtime test.

t: Gst-plugins-bad: gst-plugins-bad: missing bounds checks in mpeg ps pes header parsing
d: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-bad MPEG Program Stream demuxer and resindvd DVD-playback plugin. The PES header parsers do not adequately check remaining data before reading timestamps and optional header fields. Opening a specially crafted MPEG Program Stream file can cause an out-of-bounds read and potentially crash the application, resulting in a denial of service.

t: Gst-plugins-base: gst-plugins-base: missing bounds checks in rtcp sdes packet parsing
d: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-base RTCP SDES packet parser. A remote sender able to reach an active media session can supply a malformed SDES entry whose declared length exceeds the received packet. Missing bounds validation can cause the receiver to read beyond the packet buffer, potentially crashing the application or exposing a limited amount of process memory.

t: Session fixation in the CLI login flow allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain a user's API token
d: Session Fixation vulnerability in the CLI login flow in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an API token for another user's account via a crafted login link. Starting a CLI login with POST /api/auth/cli_session needs no authentication and returns a polling token, a confirmation URL that carries that token, and a confirmation code. When a signed-in user opens that URL and clicks Confirm, NervesHub.Accounts.verify_cli_session_token/2 creates an API token for the user's account and stores it on the login, and the next poll of GET /api/auth/cli_session/<token> returns it to whoever started the login. The confirmation code is only displayed and is never compared with anything, so it cannot show that the person confirming is the one who started the login. The confirm form carries a CSRF token and the page cannot be framed, so the attacker has to persuade the user to open the link and click the button themselves. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.5.0 before 2.5.3.

t: Missing authorization in device and deployment group page events allows view-role members to change devices and deployment groups
d: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the device and deployment group pages in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated organization member with the view role to change devices and deployment groups via LiveView events reserved for the manage role. The event handlers that add and delete device certificates, add and remove tags, overwrite or clear a device's manual location, remove a device from its deployment group, move matched devices into a deployment group or remove unmatched ones, import devices from a CSV, and start, retry or delete firmware delta builds carry out the change without calling authorized!/2, and the pages render the controls to every member. A view member can add a certificate that lets whoever holds its key connect as the device, delete a certificate so the device can no longer authenticate with it, and change which deployment group, and so which firmware release, a device receives. Everything stays within the organizations the member belongs to. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

t: Improper session invalidation keeps removed or demoted members' open pages and device consoles working at their old role
d: Improper Session Invalidation vulnerability in the dashboard pages, device console and local shell channels in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an organization member who is removed or given a lower role to keep acting at their old role through anything they had open at the time. The dashboard reads the member's role once when a page mounts, in the assign_org_to_scope hook of NervesHubWeb.Auth, and the console, local shell and device event stream channels check membership once at join. Removing a member or changing their role tells none of them, so open pages keep carrying out actions and open consoles keep running commands on the device until the page reloads or the socket disconnects. The dashboard also opens consoles over NervesHubWeb.UserSocket with a token that holds only the user's id, is accepted for 24 hours, and is not revoked by signing out, which disconnects only the session's LiveViews. Whoever holds a token taken from a page can open consoles as that user, within the user's current membership, until it expires. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

t: Mass assignment of organization, product and deployment group IDs allows users to write into other organizations and receive their firmware
d: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device forms, signing key and product forms and JITP settings in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user who manages devices in any organization to write into other organizations via submitted org_id, product_id and deployment_id fields. The device API create and update actions and the dashboard device forms pass the request parameters to NervesHub.Devices.Device.changeset/2, which casts the organization, product, deployment group and update state as given. The signing key and product forms merge the session's organization into the submitted parameters so that a submitted org_id wins, and the JITP changeset accepts any product_id. Each request requires the manage role only in the user's own organization, and any account can create one. A device placed on another organization's deployment group, or moved into its product, is sent that organization's firmware with a download URL. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization, and cannot upload firmware to it. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

t: Gst-plugins-bad: gst-plugins-bad: bounds check errors in mxf vanc packet handling
d: A flaw was found in the GStreamer gst-plugins-bad MXF plugin. Insufficient bounds checks when parsing crafted VANC data can cause an out-of-bounds read in the demuxer, while an incorrect buffer size calculation when muxing multiple ancillary packets can cause an out-of-bounds write. Processing affected content may crash the application, resulting in a denial of service.

t: Cockpit: cockpit-storaged: tang keyserver address from an untrusted luks header clevis token reaches curl's argument vector as an option
d: A flaw was found in cockpit-storaged. A Tang keyserver address read from a clevis token in a LUKS header is concatenated into curl's argument vector without a "--" separator. An address beginning with "-" is parsed by curl as an option instead of a hostname, allowing an attacker who can attach a crafted LUKS/clevis block device (for example, a local unprivileged user with an active console or desktop login session) to have an administratively-privileged Cockpit user unknowingly trigger curl option injection when editing the device's Tang keyserver settings. This can lead to arbitrary file read or write as the Cockpit session user.

t: Improper authentication lets Google sign-in and confirmation links sign users in to accounts registered with their email address by someone else
d: Improper Authentication vulnerability in Google sign-in and email confirmation in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an attacker who registers another person's email address to share that person's account once they sign in. NervesHub.Accounts.update_or_create_user_from_ueberauth/1 signs a Google user in to any account carrying the same email that is not yet linked to a Google account, links it and marks the email confirmed, without the account's owner ever having proved they own the address. NervesHubWeb.SessionController.confirm/2 likewise signs in whoever follows a confirmation link. An attacker registers the address from the sign-up form, changes their own account's email to it, or registers it as an organization admin from an invite link, and keeps the password; when the address's owner signs in with Google or follows the confirmation link, they land in that account. The Google path also creates accounts with registrations closed and never checks Google's email_verified claim, and the API's password sign-in in NervesHubWeb.API.UserController issues tokens to accounts whose email was never confirmed. The attacker gains only what the victim is granted afterwards, and nothing on accounts whose owners never use either path. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.3.

t: Incorrect authorization in the devices page bulk move allows view-role members to move devices into another organization and receive its firmware
d: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user with the manage role in one organization and only the view role in another to move devices into the second organization's product via the "Move device(s) to product" action. The target-product event in NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.Index looks the product up with NervesHub.Products.get_by_id/2, which checks that the user is a member of the product's organization at any role, and move-devices-product then changes each selected device's organization and product. The device API's move requires manage in the target organization, and an earlier fix added the check on the organization the devices leave but not on the one they enter. A moved device keeps its key and certificate, joins the target organization's matching deployment groups, and is sent their firmware with a download URL, which the view role cannot otherwise obtain. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

t: Gstreamer: gstreamer: use-after-free in gstreamer core buffer value deserialization
d: A use-after-free flaw was found in GStreamer core buffer value deserialization. When serialized buffer text contains an invalid character, an error path frees a mapped buffer before unmapping it. Applications that parse untrusted caps or structure data can reach a freed-buffer read and may crash. A network-facing GStreamer Data Protocol receiver can process such caps data without user interaction; further impact has not been established.

t: Path Traversal in Agent Memory Module of SAP Cloud SDK for Python
d: The agent_memory module accepts a caller-supplied tenant parameter in create_client(tenant=...). Prior to version 0.50.0, the tenant parameter was not validated before being used to construct filesystem paths for secret resolution. A value containing path traversal sequences (for example, attacker-corp/../victim-corp) could cause the resolved path to escape the intended directory and access another tenant's secrets under:Plain Text/etc/secrets/appfnd/hana-agent-memory/<tenant>/Successful exploitation could allow unauthorized access to another tenant's mounted credentials, including OAuth client IDs and client secrets. This vulnerability could enable cross-tenant access to sensitive credentials.

t: Information Disclosure vulnerability in SAP Cloud SDK for AI(JavaScript)

An attacker with low privileges and access to application logs or forwarded error output could obtain these credentials, but only after waiting for a suitable failure event triggered by a higher-privileged user and within the limited lifetime of the token, making exploitation complex. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to reuse the disclosed credentials against the associated SAP service, resulting in a high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability.

t: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: client-level mandatory pkce bypass via login-actions entry point

The issue occurs when a user initiates a login after visiting the password reset page, causing the system to skip mandatory security checks for Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE). This could allow an attacker who intercepts a login code to gain unauthorized access to the user's account without needing the required security verifier.

t: WPML Multilingual CMS <= 4.9.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass in Language-per-Domain SSO via 'wpml_sso_token_domain' Parameter
d: The WPML Multilingual CMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race Condition in versions up to, and including, 4.9.7. This is due to the `process_iframe_request` function's language-per-domain SSO handler generating the cross-domain sign-in token via `wp_create_nonce('wpml_sso')` on the logout landing page, where the browser has already discarded its authentication cookies — so `wp_get_session_token()` returns an empty string and the token collapses to the shared anonymous nonce for the current 12-hour tick rather than a user-bound secret — and then storing it in the `wpml_sso_user_<token>_<sha256('wpml_sso'.$domain)>` transient mapped to the victim's `user_id` with no binding to the specific sign-out action or requesting client. Because an unauthenticated attacker can independently derive the identical token by triggering the logout confirmation flow on `wp-login.php?action=logout`, and because the `is_iframe_request()` gate conditions (the per-domain SSO `started` transient and domain-hash derived from the public constant `SSO_NONCE`) are fully computable within the 60-second `SSO_TIMEOUT` window, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the forged `wpml_sso_token_domain` parameter with a `wpml_user_signed_in` status to a secondary language-domain endpoint before the legitimate `wpml_user_signed_out` iframe fires, causing WordPress authentication cookies to be issued for the victim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to gain access to accounts of users — including administrators — who are actively in the process of logging out during the race window.

t: LimeSurvey Community Edition 7.7.0 - Stored XSS in Central Participants blocklist control
d: LimeSurvey Community Edition 7.7.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Central Participants Database blocklist control. An authenticated user with only global participantpanel:import permission can import a CSV participant_id containing HTML. The import flow persists that value without model validation. When a CPDB editor opens the participant list, LimeSurvey derives ButtonGroupWidget id and name attributes from participant_id and inserts them without HTML encoding, causing attacker-controlled markup to execute in the victim's authenticated LimeSurvey origin. Exploitation can access session-exposed data and issue same-origin requests with the victim's effective permissions.

t: Improper verification of JWT signature in IASContextProvider leads to tenant/user identity spoofing ( sap-cloud-sdk (pip))
d: The SAP Cloud SDK for Python contains an improper cryptographic signature verification vulnerability (CWE-347) in IASContextProvider, the runtime-context provider registered by default via bootstrap(app).IASContextProvider extracted the app_tid, sap_gtid and user_uuid claims from the IAS JWT in the Authorization header using an unverified decoder and wrote them into the request-scoped RuntimeContext without validating the token signature. A remote caller could submit a self-signed JWT naming a victim tenant/user; the forged identity then propagated to every consumer of the runtime context:OTel span attributes (sap.tenancy.tenant_id, user.id) via RuntimeContextSpanProcessorlog records via IdentityLogFilteraudit events (tenant_id, user_initiator_id) via AuditClienttenant routing via CBCClientThis completes an earlier remediation that fixed the same unverified pattern in StarletteIASTelemetryMiddleware but did not cover IASContextProvider.

t: Cross-tenant sandbox takeover in SAP/astonish

Versa has confirmed a buffer overflow vulnerability in the IPsec implementation on VOS, aka Versa FlexVNF. Buffer Overflow Vulnerability Description When a maliciously crafted IKE Auth packet is sent to VOS, the vsmd process crashes, thereby resulting in a Denial of Service. An attacker can create a Denial-of-Service attack on the VOS appliances by crafting a malicious IKE Auth packet and sending it to the WAN interfaces on the VOS. During the IKE Authentication phase, if the IKE SA negotiation fails, and the size of the Remote ID is larger than the buffer size used to process the Remote ID, it will result in a crash of the vsmd process on the VOS appliance. What is impacted? VOS nodes configured with IPsec VPN profiles of type controller-staging-sdwan or remote-access-server using a WAN interface as the IPsec endpoint are vulnerable. (IPsec profiles configured with an overlay interface as the IPsec endpoint are not affected.) This configuration typically applies to all Controllers, Hub Controllers, and SSE Gateways. Additionally, site-to-site VPN profiles configured without a peer IP address, hostname, or FQDN are also vulnerable. What is not impacted? The VOS nodes listed above are not vulnerable if they are not accessible from the Internet.

The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. This service generates session identifiers using UUID version 1 (UUIDv1), which is derived from the system’s date and time and its MAC address. As a result, successive identifiers differ only slightly and can be predicted. An attacker who can predict a user’s session ID could hijack that user’s session. Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The /authenticate endpoint of this service passes user-supplied username and password values to child_process.exec() through a sanitizer (escapeRegExp) that removes regular expression metacharacters but not newline characters. An unauthenticated attacker can inject a newline character into the username field to execute arbitrary shell commands as the versa OS service user. No credentials are required; the attacker needs only a CSRF token, which can be obtained from an unauthenticated page load. Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The /decryptTest endpoint of this service is registered in server.js before the session authentication middleware and creates an authenticated session whenever it receives a token that decrypts successfully. Because the key and initialization vector (IV) used for decryption are hardcoded and identical across all VOS appliances, an unauthenticated attacker with network access can compute a valid token, submit it to /decryptTest, and obtain a fully authenticated session without providing any credentials. Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The express-session middleware in server.js is configured with a hardcoded secret that is identical across all VOS appliances and is used to sign session cookies. An attacker who obtains a valid session ID from any source can compute the correct HMAC-SHA256 signature and forge a session cookie that the server accepts as legitimate. Because the secret is shared across all VOS appliances, a forged cookie is accepted by any VOS appliance in the deployment. Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. This service authenticates users and administrators to its web interface during initial provisioning using default credentials and HTTP Basic Authentication. An attacker with network access who knows the default credentials could authenticate to the service and perform provisioning actions on the VOS appliance. Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

r: Smart Attendance System with QR Code Scanner

t: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Stack Buffer Underwrite via Telnet Dissector Backspace Handling
d: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains a stack buffer underwrite vulnerability in the telnet dissector in src/dissectors/ec_telnet.c that decrements the output pointer on backspace without a lower bound check. Attackers can send a telnet stream with more backspaces than preceding characters to write below the stack buffer, corrupting the stack of the Ettercap process that normally runs as root.

t: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via HTTP NTLM Authentication Parsing
d: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Parse_NTLM_Auth() in src/dissectors/ec_http.c due to unvalidated NTLM message offsets. Attackers can send a crafted HTTP Authorization header observed by Ettercap to read beyond the buffer, disclosing memory or crashing the process.

t: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Stack Buffer Overflow via WPA CCMP Decryption
d: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains an integer underflow in ccmp_decrypt() in src/ec_encryption_ccmp.c that subtracts the 8-byte CCMP trailer without checking minimum length. Attackers on a network whose WPA key is loaded can send a short crafted CCMP frame to overflow a stack buffer in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

t: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via sslw_remove_sts
d: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains an out-of-bounds read and size_t underflow vulnerability in sslw_remove_sts() in src/ec_sslwrap.c, caused by a stale length and an unchecked memmem() result when stripping Strict-Transport-Security headers. A malicious HTTPS server whose response passes through Ettercap's SSL interception can trigger out-of-bounds reads and memory corruption in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

t: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via TLS SNI Parsing
d: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in sslw_get_clienthello_sni() in src/ec_sslwrap.c that trusts the unchecked 16-bit SNI length field. Network-adjacent attackers can send crafted TLS ClientHello messages during SSL interception to leak up to 64 KB of heap memory upstream or crash Ettercap.

t: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Heap Buffer Overflow via Gadu-Gadu Dissector
d: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in gg_get_version() in src/dissectors/ec_gg.c that writes up to 44 bytes into a 30-byte allocation. Remote attackers can send Gadu-Gadu traffic on TCP port 8074 with a crafted version field through a monitored network to corrupt heap memory in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

t: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Use-After-Free via PCRE2 Filter Substitution
d: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in func_pcre() in src/ec_filter.c that reads the PCRE2 ovector after freeing match data. Network-adjacent attackers can send packets matching a loaded pcre_regex() substitution filter to corrupt memory and potentially execute code as root.

t: Fluxion before 6.39 OS Command Injection via Crafted SSID
d: Fluxion before 6.39 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the fluxion.sh target scanner, which decodes access point ESSIDs with eval after escaping only single quotes. Attackers within Wi-Fi range can broadcast an access point with a crafted SSID to execute commands as root when the operator scans or selects it.

t: Instatic before 0.0.21 Authorization Bypass via Row Author Reassignment Endpoint
d: Instatic before 0.0.21 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in handleRowAuthor that allows authenticated users to skip table-level access checks by loading rows with getDataRow() instead of loadRowForAccess(). Attackers holding content.edit.any but lacking data.system.tables.read can send PATCH requests to /admin/api/cms/data/rows/:id/author to read system-table rows and reassign their authors.

t: NocoBase plugin-ai 2.1.0 through 2.2.41 Authorization Bypass via Sub-Agent Username Override
d: NocoBase plugin-ai 2.1.0 through 2.2.41 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in getAccessibleAIEmployee() that lets authenticated users access unassigned AI employees by overriding the role-derived filter with a supplied username. Attackers can use the dispatch-sub-agent-task tool to run ungranted AI employees with their tools and permissions, and get-ai-employee to read their prompts and tool configuration.

t: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 -dSAFER Bypass via .putgstringcopy .forceput Recovery
d: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 contains a -dSAFER bypass vulnerability in the .putgstringcopy procedure in gs_fonts.ps, which calls the privileged .forceput operator without checking operand types. Attackers can supply crafted PostScript or PDF documents that trigger a type error, recover .forceput via a custom error handler, and cause a use-after-free across save/restore to execute arbitrary code.

t: Ampache before 8.4.0 Stored XSS via Song Lyrics ID3 Tag
d: Ampache before 8.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with upload rights to inject script through unescaped song lyrics in LyricsView.php getLyrics() and show_lyrics.inc.php. Attackers can upload a song whose lyrics ID3 tag contains HTML and script to execute code in the browser of any user viewing the lyrics.

t: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Use-After-Free via Stale Brush Cache Pointer
d: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in update_gdi_patblt(), update_gdi_polygon_cb() and update_gdi_mem3blt() that retain stale brush cache pointers. A malicious RDP server can resend CACHE_BRUSH to the same slot then send PATBLT, causing clients to read freed heap memory, disclosing data or crashing.

t: MailEnable Enterprise Premium before 10.62 Heap Overflow via IMAP X-FB-FETCH
d: MailEnable Enterprise Premium before 10.62 contains a heap overflow vulnerability in the IMAP X-FB-FETCH command that allows authenticated users to overflow a fixed 0x400-byte heap buffer. Attackers can supply an X-FB-USER address longer than about 1016 bytes, which is formatted without a length check, to crash the IMAP service and cause denial of service.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via BIND8 edit_recs.cgi ALL View
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in bind8/edit_recs.cgi that outputs raw DNS record values without HTML escaping in ALL view mode. Delegated zone users such as Virtualmin domain owners can store record values containing script that executes in an administrator's browser when viewing zone records.

t: Webmin through 2.670 OS Command Injection via Samba User Account Options
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in samba/save_euser.cgi that allows authenticated Samba user maintainers to inject commands via unvalidated opts parameter. Attackers can embed shell metacharacters in account option flags passed by create_user and modify_user to backquote_logged, executing commands as root.

t: Group-Office before 6.8.181, 25.0.116, and 26.0.58 Local File Read via processUploadQueue
d: Group-Office before 6.8.181, 25.0.116, and 26.0.58 contains an arbitrary local file read vulnerability in FolderController::actionProcessUploadQueue that allows authenticated users to read server files by supplying absolute paths in the blobs parameter. Attackers can have files hard-linked or copied into their own folder and downloaded, exposing other users' stored files and config.php database credentials.

t: Group-Office before 6.8.181, 25.0.116, and 26.0.58 Stored XSS via filterXSS Bypass
d: Intermesh Group-Office before 6.8.181, 25.0.116, and 26.0.58 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the email viewer due to a flawed regex in StringHelper::filterXSS. Remote attackers can send emails containing tags like svg/onload, which MessagePanel.js renders raw, executing script in the recipient's session when opened.

t: Group-Office before 6.8.181, 25.0.116, and 26.0.58 Missing Authorization in Forms Report Download
d: Intermesh Group-Office before 6.8.181, 25.0.116, and 26.0.58 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to download form reports via api/download.php without permission checks. Attackers can request the business/forms/report blob with a form ID to export every submission as an XLSX file, disclosing submissions they are not permitted to see.

t: Faveo Helpdesk through 2.0.3 Cross-Department Ticket Tampering via TicketController
d: Faveo Helpdesk through 2.0.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in TicketController that allows authenticated agents to modify tickets outside their department by referencing raw ticket IDs. Attackers can call merge-tickets, change-owner, ticket/assign and ticket/surrender endpoints to close, merge or reassign other departments' tickets and enumerate customers' ticket subjects.

t: langchain4j-aideepin through 3.32.0 IDOR via /character/message reference endpoints
d: langchain4j-aideepin through 3.32.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CharacterMessageController that allows authenticated users to access other users' message references due to missing owner checks. Attackers can supply another user's message uuid to the knowledge-embedding-ref, memory-embedding-ref, or graph-ref endpoints to retrieve knowledge-base chunks, long-term memory text, and knowledge-graph data.

t: INDOTALENT WHMS before 10.20261109 Path Traversal via FileDocument/GetDocument and FileImage/GetImage
d: INDOTALENT WHMS before 10.20261109 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read arbitrary files via the documentName and imageName parameters. Attackers can self-register and supply traversal sequences to GetDocument or GetImage, which use Path.Combine without containment checks, to read files like appsettings.json.

t: INDOTALENT WHMS before 10.20261109 Default Administrator Credentials via UserAdminSeeder
d: INDOTALENT WHMS before 10.20261109 contains a default credentials vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator access because UserAdminSeeder creates admin@root.com with password 123456. Attackers can log in with these credentials, which carry every admin role and no forced password change, to fully control deployments that kept them.

t: INDOTALENT WHMS before 10.20261109 Hard-Coded JWT Signing Key Authentication Bypass
d: INDOTALENT WHMS (Asp.Net-Core-Inventory-Order-Management-System) before 10.20261109 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability caused by a hard-coded JWT signing key, issuer and audience in appsettings.json. Unauthenticated remote attackers can forge tokens for any user ID and role that the Tokens/DI.cs validator trusts, gaining administrator access to the entire API.

t: Map-OS 5.0.0 to before 5.2.2 Privilege Escalation via /api/v1/usuarios
d: Map-OS 5.0.0 to before 5.2.2 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in the REST users API that allows non-administrator operators holding the cUsuario permission to bypass permission-delegation and super-administrator protections. Attackers can send POST, PUT, or DELETE requests to /api/v1/usuarios to assign the Administrador group, reset the super administrator password, or delete higher-privileged users.

t: DataRoom through 3.0.0 SQL Injection via MyBatisService.generateSql
d: DataRoom through 3.0.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability in MyBatisService.generateSql that allows sharer-role users to inject SQL by supplying crafted dataset parameters. Attackers can send crafted inputParam values to /dataRoom/dataset/run, exploiting unquoted string parameters or MySQL backslash escapes, to execute injected SQL against the database.

t: DataRoom through 3.0.0 Incorrect Authorization via /dataRoom/dataset/run/test
d: DataRoom through 3.0.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in DatasetController.runTest that allows visitor-role users to execute dataset definitions supplied in the request body. Attackers can specify an arbitrary dataSourceCode and raw SELECT SQL to query any configured relational data source using its stored decrypted credentials, bypassing developer-only restrictions.

t: Movim through 0.35.5 Authorization Bypass via Post::ajaxGetPost Cached Post Read
d: Movim through 0.35.5 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Post::ajaxGetPost that allows authenticated users to read restricted posts by supplying server, node and nodeid values. Attackers who know item identifiers can retrieve cached community or contact-only posts from the pod-wide cache before the XMPP authorization check runs.

t: PowerDNS-Admin before 2026.11.0 Missing Authorization via Template Apply Endpoint
d: PowerDNS-Admin before 2026.11.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the apply_records handler for /admin/template/<template>/apply that lets any authenticated User-role account modify shared zone templates. Attackers can replace a template's record set by name, injecting attacker-chosen NS, MX, A or CNAME records into every zone later created from it.

t: Pig before 4.1.2 Missing Authorization Exposes OAuth2 Client Secrets via /client
d: Pig before 4.1.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in SysClientController that allows authenticated users without client-management permission to retrieve OAuth2 client secrets via GET /client/{clientId} and GET /client/export. Attackers can fetch clientSecret values for seed clients like pig, app, and daemon or export the client table, then obtain tokens using those clients' configured grant types.

t: VanBlog through 0.54.0 Private Article Disclosure via Public Password Endpoint
d: VanBlog through 0.54.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read private and hidden articles via the POST /api/public/article/:id endpoint. Attackers can submit any non-empty password for private articles lacking an effective password, or request hidden articles, since getByIdWithPassword never checks the hidden flag, exposing full article content.

t: MrDoc through 1.1.1 Missing Authorization via Project Document Sort Handlers
d: MrDoc through 1.1.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the project_doc_sort and manage_project_doc_sort handlers that allows registered users to modify other users' documents by supplying arbitrary document IDs in sort_data. Attackers owning any project can reparent and reorder documents by sequential ID and set their status to draft or removed, hiding published documents.

t: Krayin CRM before 2.2.8 Broken Object Level Authorization via Lead Tag Attach/Detach
d: Krayin CRM before 2.2.8 contains a broken object level authorization vulnerability in Lead TagController attach and detach actions that skip the data-scope check. Authenticated users restricted to individual or group data scope can add or remove tags on leads owned by users outside their scope.

t: IETF Datatracker before 12.83.0 Cross-NomCom Authorization Bypass via Nomcom Views
d: IETF Datatracker before 12.83.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows NomCom role holders to access other committees' records by supplying sequential primary keys. Attackers can abuse view_feedback_nominee, view_feedback_topic, view_feedback_unrelated and edit_nominee to view confidential nominee identities, reclassify feedback, and change nominee email addresses.

t: REBUILD before 4.5.3 Authorization Bypass via Feeds Details and Comments Endpoints
d: REBUILD before 4.5.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in FeedsListController fetchDetails and fetchComments that skips privilege filtering and FeedsHelper.checkReadable checks. Authenticated attackers can enumerate sequential IDs via the feeds-details and comments-list endpoints to read private or team-scoped feed content, images, attachments and comments.

t: Tinyproxy through 1.11.3 Hostname ACL Allow-List Bypass via Suffix Match
d: Tinyproxy through 1.11.3 contains an access control bypass vulnerability in acl_string_processing() in src/acl.c that compares only trailing hostname characters without checking DNS label boundaries. Attackers controlling the PTR record for their source IP, such as untrusted.net, can satisfy an 'Allow trusted.net' entry to use the proxy despite deny-by-default ACLs.

t: Kubero 3.0.0 through 3.1.1 Authentication Bypass via Hardcoded JWT Secret
d: Kubero 3.0.0 through 3.1.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to forge administrative JWTs by using a hardcoded fallback signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset. Attackers can sign tokens with arbitrary role, userGroups and permissions claims, which JwtStrategy.validate() trusts without a database lookup, to take control of pipelines, applications, users and API tokens.

t: Bitpoll through 0.11.0 Unauthenticated Vote and Comment Disclosure via Unscoped Lookups
d: Bitpoll through 0.11.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read votes and comments from other polls via unscoped object lookups in views.py. Attackers can pair any public poll slug with sequential vote or comment IDs in vote, vote_delete, vote_assign, or delete_comment GET requests to read names and comments from restricted polls.

t: OmniAgent Bash Approval Gate Bypass via find -execdir in Safe-Command Allowlist
d: OmniAgent through commit 12b98c5 contains an approval bypass vulnerability in ReflexionAgent._is_safe_bash_command that treats any command starting with find as safe without inspecting -execdir arguments. Prompt-injected agents can run find with -execdir to invoke binaries like dd, nc, perl or openssl through an unsandboxed shell, overwriting files or executing code without human approval.

t: Pico through 4.1.2 SSRF in Feeds Service via run SSH Command
d: Pico through 4.1.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the feeds service that allows signed-up users to make the server fetch arbitrary URLs via the run SSH command. Attackers can upload a feeds digest post listing internal URLs and trigger immediate fetching through Fetcher.ParseURL to reach loopback, RFC1918, and cloud metadata endpoints.

t: Omnom through 0.9.0 SSRF via Add Feed /add_feed Route
d: Omnom through 0.9.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to make server requests to arbitrary hosts by submitting feed URLs to /add_feed. Attackers can supply internal addresses that getFeedInfo, gofeed ParseURL, and fetchImageAsInlineURL fetch without validation, using reflected error messages to probe internal hosts and ports.

t: DollarDollar through 4.4 Missing Authorization in /add_expense Balance Tampering
d: DollarDollar through 4.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in add_expense() that allows authenticated users to modify other users' account balances by supplying foreign account_id values. Attackers can submit sequential account_id, destination_account_id, and group_id values to /add_expense to tamper with balances and inject expenses into foreign groups with an arbitrary payer.

t: frab through 0.9.1 Privilege Escalation via conference_users_attributes in UsersController
d: frab through 0.9.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows authenticated crew users to grant themselves orga roles by submitting unchecked nested conference_users_attributes. Attackers can abuse UsersController#update or #create, which skip filter_conference_users, to gain orga on any conference and fully manage its events, schedule, reviewers and crew.

t: MikroDash before 0.8.79 SSRF via Personal Notification Channels
d: MikroDash before 0.8.79 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows any signed-in user, including the viewer role, to target internal addresses through notification channels. Attackers can set webhook or mail destinations to loopback, LAN or link-local addresses and call POST /api/notify-channels/{id}/test to probe the internal network.

t: Seahub through 14.0.10 Predictable Share Link Passwords via Batch Endpoint
d: Seahub through 14.0.10 contains a weak randomness vulnerability in MultiShareLinksBatch.post() that generates batch share link passwords using Python's non-cryptographic random.choices(). Authenticated users permitted to create share links can request many generated passwords via the multi-share-links batch endpoint, recover the Mersenne Twister state, and predict other users' share link passwords.

t: Tencent BrowserSkill through 0.4.2 Missing Authentication in Local WebSocket Transport
d: Tencent BrowserSkill through 0.4.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows local attackers to impersonate the bsk daemon because remoteSocket() connects to the loopback WebSocket without credentials or peer verification. Attackers who bind the daemon port before it starts or after it exits receive the extension's full tool surface, including evaluate, to run JavaScript through CDP in logged-in browser tabs.

t: Storyden through 1.26.16 Privilege Escalation via MANAGE_ROLES Role Assignment
d: Storyden through 1.26.16 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows users holding MANAGE_ROLES to grant the ADMINISTRATOR permission without being administrators. Attackers can call AccountAddRole on another controlled account or use RoleCreate and RoleUpdate to create administrator roles, taking full control of the instance.

t: Mediary Scout before 2026.11.05 SSRF via PanSou Search Source Setting
d: Mediary Scout before 2026.11.05 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows any authenticated user, including non-owner accounts, to set an arbitrary PanSou base URL via savePanSouBaseUrlAction without role checks. Attackers can trigger probePanSou() to send server-side POST requests to internal hosts and use distinct error responses as an oracle for internal host and port discovery.

t: Universal-modder before e88f687 Cross-Site WebSocket Command Execution via HostLink
d: Universal-modder before commit e88f6876745427321eb755ebc98276063a962d8a contains a missing WebSocket Origin validation vulnerability in the HostLink class of its passthrough example mods that allows remote attackers to execute Minecraft commands. Any web page open in the player's browser can connect cross-site to the unauthenticated loopback WebSocket and send cmd messages that WorldBridge.command() runs with operator authority.

t: Munin munin-httpd through 2.999.18 Path Traversal via Static File Handler
d: Munin munin-httpd 2.99.1 through 2.999.18 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the static file handler of Munin::Master::HTML::handle_request that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files outside the static directory. Attackers can request /static/../<file> to bypass the '/../' substring check and read munin.conf and plugin-conf.d files containing monitored service credentials.

KUSANAGI provided by GMO Prime Strategy Co., Ltd. contains an HTTP header injection vulnerability that may allow arbitrary HTTP headers to be injected into the HTTP response when a user accesses a specially crafted URL.

t: SourceCodester Smart Attendance System with QR Code Scanner Admin Account Creation create_admin.php getMessage missing authentication
d: A vulnerability has been found in SourceCodester Smart Attendance System with QR Code Scanner 1.0. This impacts the function getMessage of the file create_admin.php of the component Admin Account Creation. Such manipulation of the argument e leads to missing authentication. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

t: SQL injection leading to privilege escalation
d: An unauthenticated SQL injection can occur on the front end of any site that uses craft.search to perform a search, allowing stacked query execution and enabling escalation to an administrator. Note that this only affects MySQL/MariaDB. Impact * SQL injection — The attribute parameter is concatenated into the query unsanitized, and because PDO runs with emulated prepares, stacked statements execute. This gives unauthenticated read and write access to the application database. * Privilege escalation to administrator — The write primitive was used to set the admin flag on user ID 1 in the users table, confirmed by reading the value back. Craft short-circuits its permission checks on this single column, so no further changes were needed. The same primitive can overwrite any account’s password hash. Update to the patched versions (4.18.9 and 5.11.2) to get the fix. If you cannot update immediately, you can block front-end requests with %5Battribute%5D and [attribute] anywhere in the query string as a temporary mitigation.

t: SourceCodester Smart Attendance System with QR Code Scanner Password Reset reset_password.php password recovery
d: A flaw has been found in SourceCodester Smart Attendance System with QR Code Scanner 1.0. This affects an unknown function of the file reset_password.php of the component Password Reset. This manipulation of the argument username/password causes weak password recovery. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.
